layers.title: Shaded relief
layers.source: Shaded relief computed by terrain/hazards.py from the HiRISE terrain model (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic

layers.title: HiRISE image
layers.source: HiRISE (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic of Jezero: PSP_003798_1985_Edited_affine_25cm_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_offNadir.tif

layers.title: Slope
layers.source: Slope computed by terrain/hazards.py from the HiRISE terrain model (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic

layers.title: Thermal inertia
layers.source: THEMIS (Mars Odyssey), thermal inertia mosaic: THEMIS_TI_Mosaic_Quant_00N060E_100mpp.cub
layers.note: Values in J m^-2 K^-1 s^-1/2 are in thermal_inertia.tif (NaN = no data). Native pixels are much larger than the 5 m grid, so edges look soft.

layers.title: Minerals
layers.source: CRISM (MRO), MTRDR summary parameters, image FRT00005C5E: frt00005c5e_07_su166j_mtr3.img
layers.note: Coloured where a CRISM summary parameter passes our threshold. Thresholds were tuned by eye.

layers.title: Hazards
layers.source: Computed by terrain/hazards.py from the HiRISE terrain model (MRO) and THEMIS thermal inertia (Mars Odyssey): slope, roughness (a stand-in for rocks) and loose sand. Limits in terrain/thresholds.toml are team assumptions, not sourced NASA limits.

sources_notes.space_weather.csv: NASA DONKI (CCMC space weather database), 2025-06-01 to 2025-12-31. mars_impact comes from DONKI's own model runs and instrument lists.
sources_notes.radiation.csv: ESTIMATE, not a measurement at this site: Curiosity RAD surface average at Gale, 0.64 mSv/day (Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343). Applied unchanged at Jezero, which sits about 2 km higher than Gale crater's floor under a thinner atmosphere, so the real dose is probably somewhat higher.
sources_notes.dem.tif: HiRISE (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic of Jezero: JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40.tif
